```{julia}
using CairoMakie
using LinearAlgebra

using MMJMesh.Plots
using MMJMesh.Mathematics
```

## Approximation mit Hutfunktionen

### Funktionen

```{julia}
x = parameter(0 .. 4π)
u = cos(x)
v = 1 - x / 4π
f = u * v

fplot(u, v, f)
```

### Funktionswerte

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
x = [1, 3, 7]
y = f.(x)
p = fplot(f)
scatter!(x, y, color = :tomato)
p
```
:::

::: {.tinh-scaffold}
```{julia}
x = [1, 3, 7]
y = 0 * x
p = fplot(f)
scatter!(x, y, color = :tomato)
p
```
:::

### Approximation

Funktion

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
nodes = range(0, 4π, 6)
phis = hatfunctions(nodes)
uHat = f.(nodes)
fa = uHat ⋅ phis
fplot(fa, f)
```
:::

Fehler

```{julia}
e = f - fa
fplot(e)
```

### Norm

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
norm2(u) = sqrt(integrate(u * u, domain(u)))

norm2(e)
```
:::

### Konvergenz

Funktion um Approximationsfehler zu berechnen

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
function approximation_error(Ne)
	nodes = range(0, 4π, Ne + 1)
	phis = hatfunctions(nodes)
	fa = f.(nodes) ⋅ phis
	return norm2(f - fa)
end

approximation_error(4)
```
:::

Approximationsfehler für $4, 8, \dots, 2^{10}$ Elemente

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
Nes = 2 .^ (2:10)
hs = 4π ./ Nes
es = approximation_error.(Nes)
```
:::

Fehler über Anzahl der Elemente

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
scatterlines(Nes, es)
```
:::

Fehler über Elementgröße

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
scatterlines(hs, es)
```
:::

Mit loglog-Skala

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
fig = Figure()
Axis(fig[1, 1], xscale = log2, yscale = log10)
scatterlines!(Nes, es)
fig
```
:::

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
fig = Figure()
Axis(fig[1, 1], xscale = log2, yscale = log10)
scatterlines!(hs, es)
fig
```
:::

### Zur Interpretation von loglog-Plots

```{julia}
mks = monomials(1:4, 0.0001 .. 1)
fplot(mks...)
```

```{julia}
fig = Figure()
Axis(fig[1, 1], xscale = log10, yscale = log10)
fplot!(mks...)
fig
```

## Doppelt-logarithmische Darstellung

Verhältnis aufeinanderfolgender Fehler (Halbierung von $h$)

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
es[1:(end-1)] ./ es[2:end]
```
:::

Steigung im loglog-Plot

::: {.tinh-solution}
```{julia}
log2.(es[1:(end-1)] ./ es[2:end])
```
:::
